---
title: "Get started"
description: >
  Build the smallest complete bslibreact app: an R Shiny server and a React
  client that looks like a bslib page.
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

This article builds the smallest complete bslibreact app. The Shiny server is
written in R and does the reactive work. The page is a React client that
shows a slider in a sidebar, a value box, and a plot, all with bslib's own
markup and styling.

![The finished app: a sidebar with a slider, a value box showing the
slider's value, and a histogram.](https://www.samuelbharti.com/bslibreact/assets/hello.png)

## Requirements

- R, with the packages installed in step 1.
- A current Node.js LTS release, to build the client.
- git, to copy the example.

## 1. Install the R packages

bslibreact installs from GitHub with pak, and brings shiny and bslib with it.
shinyreact, which provides the page and the plumbing between Shiny and
React, is on CRAN.

```{r}
install.packages(c("pak", "shinyreact"))
pak::pak("samuelbharti/bslibreact/pkg-r")
```

## 2. Copy the example app

The repository holds this app as `examples/01-hello`. Clone the repository
and copy that folder:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/samuelbharti/bslibreact.git
cp -R bslibreact/examples/01-hello myapp
cd myapp
```

The folder has two halves:

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `app.R` | The Shiny server. It holds reactive code only. |
| `src/App.tsx` | The React client. It lays out the page. |
| `src/ui.tsx` | Mounts `App` on the page. It is the same in every app. |
| `vite.config.ts` | Builds `src/` into `www/ui.js`. |
| `www/ui.js` | The built client that the server sends to the browser. |

`app.py` is the same server in Python. Delete it if the app only needs R.

## 3. Read the server

`app.R` has no layout code. Its page is shinyreact's `page_react()`, and
`page_deps()` gives that page the CSS and JavaScript a bslib page would
attach on its own.

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(shinyreact)

app_theme <- bs_theme(version = 5)

ui <- page_react(
  title = "Hello bslibreact",
  theme = app_theme,
  bslibreact::page_deps(app_theme)
)
```

The server function then does three things.

```{r}
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  bslibreact::host_input(
    output,
    "bins",
    shiny::sliderInput("bins", "Bins", min = 1, max = 50, value = 30)
  )

  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    req(input$bins)
    hist(rnorm(500), breaks = input$bins, col = "#447099", border = "white")
  })

  output$bins_count <- renderText({
    req(input$bins)
    input$bins
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

`host_input()` renders a real `sliderInput()` on the server and hosts it for
the client to display, so the slider keeps the look and behaviour Shiny gives
it. The client mounts it under the id `bins_ui`, and the server reads its
value as `input$bins`, as in any Shiny app.

`output$plot` and `output$bins_count` are ordinary Shiny outputs. Both start
with `req(input$bins)`, because a hosted slider has no value until the
client has mounted it.

## 4. Read the client

`src/App.tsx` is the whole page. Each component reproduces the markup of one
bslib or Shiny call.

```tsx
import {
  PageSidebar,
  SliderInput,
  PlotOutput,
  ValueBox,
  TextOutput,
  useShinyInitialized,
} from "bslibreact";

export default function App() {
  const ready = useShinyInitialized();
  if (!ready) return null;

  return (
    <PageSidebar title="Hello bslibreact" sidebar={<SliderInput id="bins_ui" />}>
      <ValueBox title="Bins">
        <TextOutput id="bins_count" className="value-box-value" />
      </ValueBox>
      <PlotOutput id="plot" height="400px" />
    </PageSidebar>
  );
}
```

The ids connect the two halves:

| Client | Server |
| --- | --- |
| `<SliderInput id="bins_ui" />` | `host_input(output, "bins", sliderInput("bins", ...))` |
| `<PlotOutput id="plot" />` | `output$plot <- renderPlot(...)` |
| `<TextOutput id="bins_count" />` | `output$bins_count <- renderText(...)` |

A hosted input always carries the `_ui` suffix on the client. `bins` is the
slider's own input id, so the element that hosts it needs a different one.

## 5. Build the client

```bash
npm install
npm run build
```

`npm install` fetches the `bslibreact` npm package, and the build writes
`www/ui.js`. While developing, `npm run dev` rebuilds on every change to
`src/`.

## 6. Run the app

```{r}
shiny::runApp(".")
```

The browser opens the page in the screenshot above. Move the slider, and the
value box and the histogram both update.
